title: Is World War III Already Here? — with Lieutenant General H. R. McMaster
summary: A former US national security adviser describes Russian and Chinese information warfare and Chinese coercion below the threshold of war as an unrecognised war against the US.

assertions.quote: we're currently in a war that we don't even recognize
Russia doesn't create the divisions in our society but they're doing everything they can to to widen those gaps among Americans

verdicts.note: US intelligence, Senate reports and platform takedowns document Russian troll and bot campaigns aimed at polarising US and European audiences.
DDIS reports Russian influence operations via online platforms and agents since 2022, aimed at sowing discord in Europe and weakening support for Ukraine.
US intelligence lists disinformation and influence operations among Russia's gray-zone tools, often denied; social media are not named specifically.
The Bulletin says Russia and China have used deepfakes and social media in wide-ranging disinformation campaigns; it does not spell out an aim of dividing Western publics.

assertions.quote: Russia doesn't care who wins our elections what they really care about is that a large number of Americans doubt the legitimacy of the result

verdicts.note: Undermining trust was a documented aim, but the 2017 US intelligence assessment also found a clear Russian preference for one candidate in 2016.

assertions.quote: these were specific uses of information space to reduce will and to set conditions for physical aggression

verdicts.note: Cyber and information operations accompanied Russian moves on Georgia in 2008, Crimea in 2014 and Ukraine in 2022.
DDIS says Russian hacking of transport and energy systems likely seeks access it could use to disable critical infrastructure immediately before or during a war against NATO.
US intelligence documents Russia's cyber attacks and influence operations below the level of armed conflict, but does not describe them as preparing the ground for military aggression.

assertions.quote: they want to accomplish their objectives below the level of what might elicit a concerted military response from us

verdicts.note: Trade punishment of Australia, Lithuania and South Korea and maritime militia pressure are documented grey-zone tactics.

DoD 2025 documents China using market access, trade, investment and supply chains to coerce opponents 'without resorting to military action', e.g. tariffs on Taiwan goods and import bans to push Guatemala to drop Taiwan.

DDIS: China relies primarily on economic power, deliberately increases other countries' dependence (rare earths, batteries, solar) to gain influence and deter sanctions, and pressures Taiwan below the threshold of war.
US intelligence describes China's multidomain coercion of Japan after Takaichi's remarks: cancelled flights and exchanges, a seafood ban, possible further economic measures, all short of war.

assertions.quote: this is a unprecedented military buildup not unprecedented but maybe at least going back to the 30s

verdicts.note: China's navy is the world's largest by hull count, its defence budget has grown for three decades and its nuclear arsenal is expanding fast, per US and independent assessments.

SIPRI records China's spending rising for 31 consecutive years, the longest streak in its database, to fund a comprehensive PLA modernization by 2035, including sixth-generation fighters and a strategic bomber.
DoD 2025 calls it 'China's historic military buildup': a large and growing nuclear, maritime, long-range strike, cyber and space arsenal that leaves the US homeland increasingly vulnerable.

DDIS: China now has the world's largest navy by number of warships, builds about three times as many warships a year as the US on a third of its budget, and has expanded rocket, naval and air forces since 2000.

assertions.quote: they'll liberalize their economy and they'll liberalize their form of governance okay I don't think that was ever going to be the case

verdicts.note: Two decades after WTO entry China's one-party rule has tightened under Xi rather than liberalised.

assertions.quote: I think authoritarian regimes are brittle

verdicts.note: Personalist autocracies do collapse suddenly, but many one-party regimes have proved durable for decades.
